message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 70 million years ago. It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group of early placental mammals that gave rise to both the carnivores (lion) and the perissodactyls (zebra).
